# Introduction 

The following document is the specification of the REST API for Cost management. It includes the model definition as well as all available operations. Possible actions are creating, updating, deleting and retrieving a Cost instance.

The Cost Management API provides a standardized mechanism for creating a cost instance with all the necessary cost attributes. The API consists of a simple set of operations that can interact with various components in the ODA function blocks

There are two types of costs defined in the Cost Management API:

- Projected Costs

    - Projected costs refer to estimated or forecasted expenses that are anticipated to be incurred in the future

- Actual Costs

    - Actual costs represent the real, verified expenses that have been incurred and recorded.

Projected costs are estimates of future expenses made during the planning phase, while actual costs are the realized and verified expenses based on factual data.

A Cost is made up of one or more Cost Items. There are three cycles for Cost Item:

- One Time Cost
- Recurring fixed Cost
- Consumption based cost

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Use Cases 

A cost instance is created to capture the expense (projected or actual) needed to be spent by the service provider to acquire, execute, produce, activate, operate or qualify the entity (project, service, product, resource etc). It encompasses the amount of money (forecasted or incurred) needed in, for example (not exhaustive):

- service fulfilment process, including materials, labour, overhead costs, 3rd party, and any other expenses directly associated with the acquisition of a service
- service qualification process, including materials, labour, overhead costs, and any other expenses directly associated with qualifying a service
- service discovery process, that is, the cost returned to requesting entity for the various candidate target service and resources
- project delivery, including resources time, materials, overhead costs, etc
- resource acquisition process, licenses, materials, labour, overhead costs, etc
- marketing, advertising, sales & disctribution, support staff costs, etc. In turn, the costs can be used to derive pricing, perform revenue assurance activities and produce financial reports etc.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a ProjectedCost and ActualCost inheriting properties from the abstract Cost entity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of Cost instances some may be instances of ProjectedCost where other could be instances of ActualCost. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an CostRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as ProjectedCostRef or ActualCostRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

## STATE LIFECYCLE 

## ActualCostItem state lifecycle

Following are the available state values for an actual cost item. The state graphic gives an overview of the allowed state changes

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

The following table provides the actual cost item state explanation:

| State | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| incurred | This is an initial state of an actual cost item that typically occurswhen the cost is first acquired, such as when an invoice isreceived, or a transaction is processed. |
| verified | This state indicates that an actual cost item has been reviewed,validated, and confirmed as accurate and legitimate. Thisverification process involves ensuring that the cost aligns with theorganization’s policies, procedures, and financial records. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| State | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| disputed | This state indicates that an actual cost item may not be legitimateaccording to established rules, regulations or contractualagreements. |
| allocated | This state indicates that an actual cost item has been assigned orallocated to the appropriate accounting categories, cost centers,projects, or accounts within the organization’s financial structure. |
| cancelled | This state indicates the actual cost item will not be assigned orallocated to the appropriate accounting categories, cost centers etcas the actual cost item has been cancelled. |

## ActualCost state lifecycle

Following are the available state values for an actual cost. The state graphic gives an overview of the allowed state changes

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

The following table provides the actual cost state explanation:

| State | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| inProgress | The actual cost instance has been generated and some actual costitems are yet to be assoicated to the Actual Cost instance. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| State | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| pendingAllocation | All cost items are assoicated to Actual Cost instance. However, notall the actual cost items have reached allocated or cancelled state. |
| allocated | At least one actual cost item has reached allocated state. Theremaining actual cost items are cancelled state. |
| cancelled | All the actual cost state items have reached cancelled state. |

## ProjectedCostItem state lifecycle

Following are the available state values for an projected cost item. The state graphic gives an overview of the allowed state changes

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

The following table provides the acprojectedtual cost item state explanation:

| State | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| estimated | This state indicates that the expenses for the projected cost itemhave been estimated by the cost provider and is ready forapproval. |
| reviewed | This state indicates that the expenses for the projected cost itemhave been reviewed. |
| approved | This state indicates that the expenses for the projected cost itemhave been approved. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| State | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| rejected | This state indicates that the expenses for the projected cost itemhave been rejected. |
| cancelled | This state indicates that the expenses for the projected cost itemhave been cancelled. |
| expired | This state indicates the duration for approval/rejection byconsuming stakeholder has passed and the projected cost item isexpired. |

## ProjectedCost state lifecycle

Following are the available state values for an projected cost. The state graphic gives an overview of the allowed state changes

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

The following table provides the actual cost state explanation:

| State | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| inProgress | The project cost instance has been generated and some projectcost items are yet to be assoicated to the Projected Cost instance. |
| pendingApproval | All cost items are assoicated to Projected Cost instance. Not all theprojected cost items have reached a terminal state. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| State | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| approved | At least one projected cost item has reached approved state. Theremaining projected cost items are expired, rejcted or cancelledstate. |
| cancelled | There are no projected cost items that are approved. The projectedcost items are either in expired, rejected or cancelled state. |

**Field descriptions**

**ProjectedCost fields**

| attachment | An AttachmentRefOrValue. The attachments pertaining to thecost. |
| --- | --- |
| certaintyLevel | A String. Indicates the extent of confidence in the accuracy andreliability of the projected cost estimates. Example values can be- 'Indicative cost' an early-stage estimate used to provide apreliminary idea of potential costs. 'Firm cost' also known asfixed cost or committed cost: represents a cost estimate that hasundergone detailed analysis, validation, and approval. It isconsidered highly reliable and stable. |
| costRelationship | A CostRelationship. A list of cost relationships (CostRelationship\[\*\]). Describes links with other cost(s). |
| creationDate | A DateTime. The date when the cost object is created. |
| description | A String. Free-text description of the Cost. |
| externalIdentifier | An ExternalIdentifier. A list of external identifiers assoicated withthis cost. |
| href | A String. Hyperlink reference. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| id  | A String. Unique identifier. |
| --- | --- |
| lastUpdate | A DateTime. The date when the cost object is last updated. |
| name | A String. Name of the Cost. |
| note | A Note. A list of notes made on this Cost. |
| projectedCostItem | A ProjectedCostItem. A list of Projected Cost Items items whichare part of the overall projected cost. |
| relatedEntity | A RelatedEntityRefOrValue. A list of related entity in relation tothis cost. |
| relatedParty | A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef. A list of related partyreferences playing a role in this cost object ( e.g. - ProjectManager, accountant, Procurement Officer, external vendor etc.). |
| state | A ProjectedCostStateType. Possible values for the state of theprojected cost. ENUMERATED with values:\* inProgress\* pendingApproval\* approved\* cancelled |
| validFor | A TimePeriod. A period of time, either as a deadline(endDateTime only) a startDateTime only, or both. |
| version | A String. The version of the Cost. |
| @baseType | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class. |
| @schemaLocation | A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that defines additionalattributes and relationships. |
| @type | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-classExtensible name. |

## Notification Resource Models

### 8 notifications are defined for this API.

### Notifications related to ActualCost:

- Create Event
- Delete Event

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Attribute Value Change Event
- State Change Event Notifications related to ProjectedCost:
- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event
- State Change Event The notification structure for all notifications in this API follow the pattern depicted by the figure below. A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence (eventId), an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This notification structure owns an event payload structure ("SpecificEventPayload" placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

# API OPERATIONS 

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| Operation on Entities | Uniform API Operation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrieve arepresentation of a resource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to create anew resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used to partiallyupdate a resource |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on an Entity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used to executeTask Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

## Operations on ActualCost

### List or find ActualCost objects

```
GET /actualCost?fields=…
```

**Description**

This operation list ActualCost entities. Attribute selection is enabled for all first level attributes. Filtering may be available depending on the compliance level supported by an implementation.

**Usage samples**

Here's an example of a request for retrieving multiple actual cost instances, in this example allocated actual cost instances are filtered and id, href, name and state fields need to be returned

**Request**

```
GET /actualCost?state=allocated&fields=id,name,state,hrefContent-Type: application/json
```

### Updates partially a ActualCost

### PATCH /actualCost/{id}?fields=…

### Description

This operation allows partial updates of an ActualCost entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |

| attachment |  |
| costRelationship |  |
| description |  |
| externalIdentifier |  |
| name |  |
| note |  |
| period |  |
| relatedEntity |  |
| relatedParty |  |

| version |  |

### Updates partially a ProjectedCost

### PATCH /projectedCost/{id}?fields=…

### Description

This operation allows partial updates of a ProjectedCost entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| creationDate |  |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| lastUpdate |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| attachment |  |
| certaintyLevel |  |
| costRelationship |  |
| description |  |
| externalIdentifier |  |
| name |  |
| note |  |
| projectedCostItem |  |
| relatedEntity |  |
| relatedParty |  |
| state |  |
| validFor |  |
| version |  |

    "@type": "ProjectedCost",

# API NOTIFICATIONS 

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample REST notification POST calls.

It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in the REST Guidelines reproduced below.

## Register listener

**POST /hub**

**Description**

Sets the communication endpoint address the service instance must use to deliver information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.

**Request**

```
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
```

**Response**

```
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
{
    "id":"42",
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com",    "query":""
}
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Unregister listener

**DELETE /hub/{id}**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

**Request**

```
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
```

**Response**

```
204
```

## Publish Event to listener

**POST /client/listener**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.

Provides to a registered listener the description of the event that was raised. The /client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

**Request**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
    "event": {
        EVENT BODY    },
    "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"
}
```

**Response**

```
201
```

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST Design Guidelines.
